label: early original-phase inputs of w/d/c/0/e/b/u/a
explanation: 93% of activation mass falls in the original (input) phase, peaking at t=2-4. The unit is driven by the current input token: w is strongest (36% rate, 25% of mass), then d, c, 0, e, b, u, a. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of the token (91% of mass). Magnitude depends on context: the top activations come in sequences that start with r/l/y/p (e.g. r r i [w] ...). Having seen r/l/y/p/2/1/g earlier raises precision only a little (F1 0.46-0.49). It fires weakly on <DEL> and on the first copy outputs, and almost never at recall_idx >= 3. Precision is low (~0.35): the same tokens often fail to fire in other contexts. That suggests a graded hidden-state readout that a token/position predicate does not fully capture. Dev split: F1 0.45, mass recall 0.77.
